## Review

AC1–AC3 are testable and unambiguous: given concrete `x, lo, hi` values, each has a single determinable expected output, including the boundary cases (`x == lo`, `x == hi` are covered by AC3's inclusive bounds).

AC4 is not testable. "Handles invalid ranges appropriately" doesn't specify:
- What counts as an invalid range (presumably `lo > hi`, but that's not stated).
- What "appropriately" means — raise an exception (which one?), swap `lo`/`hi`, return `x` unchanged, return `lo`, return `None`?

A reviewer or test-writer cannot derive a single expected behavior from this criterion, so it can't be turned into a pass/fail test case as written.

Also worth flagging: no criterion specifies behavior for non-comparable or NaN-like inputs (e.g., mixed types, `float('nan')`), though that may be out of scope depending on the intended use — worth an explicit statement either way (e.g., "type/NaN handling is out of scope for v1").

**Suggested fix for AC4**, e.g.:
> AC4: raises `ValueError` when `lo > hi`.

or, if swap-on-invalid is the intended design:
> AC4: when `lo > hi`, treats the effective bounds as `(hi, lo)` (i.e., swaps them) before applying AC1–AC3.

Either is fine — the point is the spec must commit to one behavior.

## Verdict
REVISE — AC4 must specify the exact invalid-range condition and the exact required behavior before this can be implemented or tested unambiguously.
